_doc: STEM-owned catalog for scripts/retro-topics.py. Project topics and overrides go to retro-topics.local.json (same id replaces, disabled:true removes). Thresholds are initial values reasoned in the 'why' fields (grade G1, re-measure after two retros); change them in the local file, not here.

topics.title: Question and optimize the current project process
topics.ask: Which steps of the current process cost more than they return (evidence: task notes, Learning lines, metrics)? Name one to simplify, automate or drop.
topics.why: Retros run at about 8 Done tasks; 15 means roughly every second retro, often enough to notice drift, rare enough not to become a loop.

topics.title: Question the skills in use and look for better ones
topics.ask: Which skills were used, which never? Which skill step was skipped or too long? Do official or well-known skill collections now offer a skill that does a project task better (note source, license, version)?
topics.why: Skill catalogs change slowly; 30 days matches monthly checks. Unused-skill detection needs transcripts and stays with context-report.py in the retro.

topics.title: Find information stored twice and decide where it belongs
topics.ask: Which facts appear in more than one file (AGENTS.md, rules, skills, README, handoff)? For each: the one authoritative place; remove or point the others.
topics.why: AGENTS.md is loaded every session and has a 6 KB limit; above 90 % of it, new text can only fit by moving or deleting existing text.

topics.title: Harmonize git state and question the process used with the repository
topics.ask: What is uncommitted or unpushed and why? Do commits, branches and task IDs match how the work is really done? What should change in the git workflow?
topics.why: More than 3 uncommitted files plus unpushed commits means work is no longer reviewable in task-sized pieces (R-STATE-COHERENCE).

topics.title: Too many open tasks: clean up the backlog
topics.ask: Which To Do tasks are obsolete, duplicates or too vague? Close, merge or sharpen them; keep only what can start soon.
topics.why: Session start lists only about 10 ready tasks; beyond 20 the backlog stops being read and its upkeep costs more than it helps.

topics.title: Too many tasks in progress: how to finish faster
topics.ask: Why does each In Progress task stay open (missing evidence, waiting, scope)? Finish, split, park or drop each; what keeps new ones from piling up?
topics.why: A single person or agent rarely works on more than 3-5 things at once; above 5 the tasks are waiting, not progressing.

topics.title: Vision and milestones: derive, refresh or rethink
topics.ask: Is there a current vision (audience, value, non-goals)? Do the milestones still describe the next steps and have ready tasks? Draft or derive what is missing.
topics.why: Missing vision or a milestone without To Do tasks leaves the roadmap rule (R-ROADMAP) without input; 60 days without change is about two milestone cycles.

topics.title: Is the file structure and process easy for an LLM to work through?
topics.ask: Where did an agent load too much, miss a rule or search too long? Which file is too large or ambiguous? Split, index or shorten it.
topics.why: Instruction files grow by accretion; 20 % growth since the last look is large enough to change loading cost and small enough to catch early.

topics.title: New technical options of the used LLM harnesses for more determinism
topics.ask: Which new hooks, settings, permissions or skill features of Claude Code, Codex or Copilot could replace a written rule with a machine check? Check release notes, adopt only with a concrete use.
topics.why: A changed CLI version is the cheapest local sign of new features; 30 days is the fallback when the CLI is missing or offline.

topics.title: Which instructions could be made deterministic?
topics.ask: Which rules in the process, AGENTS.md or other procedures were skipped or depend on judgment although a script, hook, template or test could enforce them? Pick the most skipped one.
topics.why: Two Learning notes about a skipped or ignored rule since the last time show a pattern, not an accident; 45 days is the fallback.
